title: Signal Weave: Canary Tuning & Cross-Functional Run Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working, pragmatic playbook for tuning canaries and coordinating cross-functional rollouts for LLM-backed features using a composite signal approach ("Signal Weave"). Aim: make activation decisions faster, reduce oscillation, and provide clear atomic rollback criteria for product, SRE, model ops, and CS.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Combine heterogeneous signals (latency, cost-per-token, quality evals, safety hits, error rates) into a single composite canary score.
- Anchor microcohorts and maintain a stable baseline by synthetic probes and pinned eval prompts.
- Use a 3-tier status (green / amber / red) with concrete numeric triggers and automated actions.
- Keep cross-functional communication template ready: who is paged, who authorizes rollforward/rollback, and what telemetry must be posted before changes.

Notes to self / context:
- Derived from past incidents where short-lived p95 regressions + noisy safety hits caused spurious rollbacks. We need smoothing + human-in-loop for ambiguous amber cases.
- This doc focuses on observability-first patterns (ideally under eng-observability) but expects product and model teams to own quality eval sets.

Signal weave design (how we stitch signals):
1) Core signals (real-time telemetry):
   - Latency: p50, p95, p99 for inference endpoint (ms).
   - Errors: 5xxs, model timeouts, truncated responses.
   - Cost per request: token_count * token_price_estimate (USD).
   - Throttles / rate-limits: count of requests hitting quota.
2) Quality signals (near-real-time / batched):
   - Eval-set pass-rate: percent of golden prompts that produce acceptable answers (daily).
   - Regression delta: relative drop vs baseline for key prompts (rolling 24h).
   - Safety hits: moderation classifier rate, broken out by category.
3) Behavioral signals (heuristic / inferred):
   - Hallucination proxy: fraction of outputs with high OOV or low factuality score from downstream reranker.
   - Response length drift: sudden median token-length change can indicate model/tokenizer issues.
   - Rerank fallback rate: how often secondary model is used.

Weighting and composite score:
- Assign baseline weights (custom per feature): latency 0.25, errors 0.25, quality 0.35, safety 0.15. (These are starting points; product teams override.)
- Normalize each signal to 0..1 where 0 = baseline best, 1 = severe.
- Composite_score = sum(weight_i * norm_signal_i).
- Map composite_score to status: 0-0.35 = green, 0.35-0.6 = amber, >0.6 = red.

Anchoring microcohorts and avoiding oscillation:
- Microcohort anchoring rule: for the first 48 hours of a rollout window, require both composite_score AND stable synthetic-probe pass-rate. Synthetic probes: pinned prompts (20-30) run every 5 minutes against canary and control.
- Smoothing: use exponential moving average on composite score (alpha = 0.25) to prevent spikes from flipping status immediately.
- Minimum exposure step: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum dwell time 30 minutes at each step and 3 consecutive probe cycles showing green/amber tolerance before moving.

Triggers and automated responses:
Green: continue. Auto-escalation—post status to #release-orchestra with baseline metrics.
Amber: hold exposure increase; auto-create post to rollout thread + page oncall. Requires a short post-mortem note from steward within 30 minutes.
Red: automatic partial rollback to last stable model variant (if available) and page SRE/product/model-ops; open P0 incident if errors>0.5% or safety hits increased >5x baseline.

Operational checklist for steward (pre-rollout):
- Confirm eval-set owner and that eval-set was run in preflight (link to timestamped results).
- Ensure synthetic-probe group is configured and compare canary vs control baseline for last 72h.
- Verify alerting: dashboards linked, PagerDuty playbook updated, Slack channel ready.
- Confirm fallback variant exists and is warmed (if required for fast rollback).
- Post rollout plan in release thread with step schedule and named guardians (product, model, SRE).

During rollout (runbook):
- Start at 1% for 30m. At 30m: run signal-weave dashboard check and synthetic probe diff. If green -> increase. If amber -> hold and escalate to human review. If red -> rollback.
- For amber cases: run narrower isolation experiments (e.g., divert 100% of a small cohort to canary for deeper telemetry).
- Keep a live log snippet in the release thread: actions taken, metric snapshots, notable anomalous traces, first-alert timestamp.

Rollback decision criteria (concrete examples):
- Latency p95 > baseline * 1.6 sustained for 10m AND composite_score > 0.6 -> immediate rollback.
- Safety hits > baseline * 3 in 15m window OR any single critical safety category spike (e.g., explicit content) -> immediate rollback + incident.
- Eval-set pass-rate drops by >8 percentage points vs baseline over 1h -> hold and remediate (rollback optional depending on product impact).

Pager and comms template (post to thread when amber/red):
- Subject: [Rollout][AMBER] feature-name - canary @ X%
- Snapshot: composite_score: 0.48; latency_p95: 520ms (+45%); eval_pass_rate: -4.2pp
- Immediate ask: SRE to check infra traces, ModelOps to look at recent model diff, Product to confirm risk tolerance.
- Owner: Priya (steward); oncall: SRE_Oncall; model: Sofia.

Synthetic probe examples (starter set):
- 10 factual prompts covering date-sensitive facts (to catch knowledge cutoff regressions).
- 10 instruction-following prompts tuned for expected feature behavior.
- 5 safety edge prompts (adversarial style) to catch simple regression in filters.
- Run frequency: every 5 minutes. Compare canary vs control; look at similarity metrics (embedding cosine) and pass flags.

Monitoring queries (examples to paste into dashboards):
- Prometheus-style latency series: rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) -> compute p95.
- Error counts: sum(rate(inference_errors_total{job=prod}[$WINDOW])) by (error_code).
- Synthetic probe passrate (BQ): SELECT COUNTIF(pass) / COUNT(1) FROM probes WHERE variant='canary' AND ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)

Post-rollout actions and postmortem checklist: 
- If rollback happened: collect first-alert traces, full eval-set diffs, and synthetic probe logs. Draft a 24h postmortem and link to confluence.
- If rollout succeeded: capture final composite_score trend, remove canary-specific dashboards, and schedule a 7-day quality review with the model/product owners.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (for later discussion):
- Best practice for weighting quality vs latency for UX-heavy features vs cost-sensitive features. (Proposed: product to supply a weight profile at feature creation.)
- How to encode human overrides safely (one-click allowlist that requires two approvers?).
- Should we automatically warm fallback GPUs before step increase or rely on fast image swap? Cost tradeoff.

Appendix: quick templates
- Rollout preflight checklist (copyable):
  * Eval-set run: URL
  * Fallback variant: name & version
  * Synthetic probe group: id
  * PagerDuty incident template: INF-XXXX
  * Stakeholders: product, modelops, SRE, CS

- Slack message template (use in #release-orchestra):
  "Rolling feature-X -> 5% canary. Steward: @Priya. Synthetic probes live: probe-23. Dashboard: <link>. Will hold 30m before next step. If amber/red, will page SRE and modelops."

- Minimal telemetry snapshot to paste (copy-pasteable):
  composite_score: 0.28
  latency_p95: 320ms (+12%)
  eval_pass_rate_delta: -1.2pp
  safety_hit_rate: 0.03%
  error_rate: 0.02%

Contact/owners:
- Priya Nair (eng-observability) - stewarding the Signal Weave prototype
- Sofia Martinez (model-ops) - eval sets & quality owner
- Liam O'Connor (SRE) - infra & oncall contact

References and tickets:
- INF-1421 (Signal Weave prototype infra work)
- confluence:rollout-signal-weave-v1 (design doc)
- github: telemetry PR 233 (dashboard + alerting rules)

End notes: this is intentionally concise and tactical. Iterate this doc against two real rollouts (Q1 experiments) and capture deviations and false-positive/negative cases in a retrospective.
